newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Cuba proposal for trade in sea turtles opposed.
newsitem.headline: Cuba proposal for trade in sea turtles opposed.

text.p: An environmental pressure group urged a world conference on Monday to reject a proposal by Cuba to trade in sea turtles, also called hawksbills.

Species Survival Network, grouping over 40 organisations, said in recommendations to a 10-day Convention on Trade in Endangered Species (CITES) ending on Friday that Havana's proposal would endanger sea turtles not just around its territory but in the whole Caribbean.
"The numbers they are working on have not been scientifically proven and the world must not take a chance," Juan Carlos Cantu, an SSN spokesman, told a press briefing.

Cuba is seeking support from CITES to harvest for trade some sea turtles around its shores, saying its strict management of domestic fishing over the last 28 years proved that the rare species' future could be guaranteed.
It says it would subject the sea turtle industry to rigorous inspection by CITES if the world was in doubt.
But SSN said illegal trade in the sea turtle was already thriving, and opening up a legal market would stimulate demand and threaten survival.

"The exploitation of hawksbill sea turtles in Cuba would curtail the ongoing intensive conservation efforts of Caribbean nations trying to protect their hawksbill populations," said another group at the conference, the Washington-based Center for Marine Conservation.
The 138-member CITES meeting in Harare will vote on the issue later this week.
